rag_sources.title: CDC Emergency Department Triage Protocols & Red-Flag Criteria
rag_sources.content: # CDC Emergency Department Triage Protocols & Red-Flag Criteria

rag_sources.title: 1. Acute Myocardial Infarction & Coronary Distress
rag_sources.content:
- **Primary Symptoms**: Retrosternal chest pain or substernal crushing pressure lasting >10 minutes, pain radiating to left shoulder, arm, neck, or jaw.
- **Associated Markers**: Diaphoresis, dyspnea, nausea, syncope.
- **Action**: Immediate EMS dispatch (911/112). Patient should remain seated. Administer non-enteric aspirin (160-325 mg chewed) if no contraindications exist. Prepare for immediate ACLS cardiac catheterization.

rag_sources.title: 2. Stroke & Acute Neurological Deficits (FAST Protocol)
rag_sources.content:
- **F - Facial Droop**: Asymmetry when smiling.
- **A - Arm Drift**: One arm drifts downward when raised.
- **S - Speech Difficulty**: Slurred, garbled, or absent speech.
- **T - Time to Act**: Emergency transport within 3-4.5 hours tPA thrombolytic window.
- **Red Flag**: Sudden severe "thunderclap" headache, hemiparesis, or unprovoked seizure requires emergency CT brain scan.

rag_sources.title: 1. Acute Upper Respiratory Infections & Seasonal Influenza
rag_sources.content:
Acute respiratory tract infections are classified based on anatomical location and severity of symptoms:
- **Mild URI**: Mild fever (<38.5°C), rhinorrhea, sore throat, cough without dyspnea. Recommended management includes oral fluid rehydration, rest, and temperature monitoring.
- **Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI)**: Fever >=38.5°C accompanied by shortness of breath, tachypnea (respiratory rate >30 breaths/min in adults), or arterial oxygen saturation (SpO2) <92%. Immediate triage to emergency facility required.

rag_sources.title: 2. Antihistamines & Oral Decongestants
rag_sources.content:
- **Cetirizine / Loratadine**: Second-generation non-drowsy antihistamines for allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
- **Saline Nasal Irrigation**: Warm 0.9% sodium chloride saline rinses for acute sinonasal congestion.

rag_sources.title: 2. Pediatric Febrile Illness Protocol
rag_sources.content:
- **Infants <3 Months**: Any fever >=38.0°C (100.4°F) is a medical emergency requiring urgent septic workup and lumbar puncture evaluation.
- **Children 3-36 Months**: Fever >=39.0°C (102.2°F) with lethargy, poor capillary refill (>2 seconds), stiff neck, or petechial rash signals bacterial meningitis or sepsis. Immediate pediatric ER transfer mandatory.

- **Action**: Immediate EMS dispatch (911/112). Patient should remain seated. Administer non-enteric aspirin (160-325 mg chewed) if no contraindications exist. Prepare for immediate ACLS cardiac catheterization.

rag_sources.title: 1. Severe Hemorrhage & Bleeding Control
rag_sources.content:
- **Direct Pressure**: Apply direct, uninterrupted firm pressure directly over the wound using sterile gauze or clean cloth.
- **Tourniquet**: If direct pressure fails to stop arterial spurting blood on limbs, apply a commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to the wound (avoiding joints).
- **Elevation**: Maintain pressure and keep the bleeding limb elevated above heart level if no fractures are suspected.

rag_sources.title: 2. Stroke & Acute Neurological Deficits (FAST Protocol)
rag_sources.content:
- **F - Facial Droop**: Asymmetry when smiling.
- **A - Arm Drift**: One arm drifts downward when raised.
- **S - Speech Difficulty**: Slurred, garbled, or absent speech.
- **T - Time to Act**: Emergency transport within 3-4.5 hours tPA thrombolytic window.
- **Red Flag**: Sudden severe "thunderclap" headache, hemiparesis, or unprovoked seizure requires emergency CT brain scan.

rag_sources.title: 1. Antipyretics & Analgesics
rag_sources.content:
- **Acetaminophen (Paracetamol)**: Dosage 500-1000 mg every 4-6 hours as needed (maximum 4000 mg/24 hours for adults). Do not combine with alcohol or hepatotoxic agents.
- **Ibuprofen (NSAID)**: Dosage 200-400 mg every 4-6 hours with food. Contraindicated in active peptic ulcer disease, severe renal failure, or third-trimester pregnancy.
